approachQuestion.prompt:
Readings across channels

A read-only r by c matrix has each row independently sorted in nondecreasing order. Rows have no ordering relationship. Given x, return whether any cell equals x. 1 <= r,c <= 1000. Use a method that treats rows independently, without building a cross-row index. Examples: [[1,8],[2,4]], x=2 -> true; x=7 -> false. Minimize worst-case probes under that row-independent restriction.
constraints: Use only the stated input ordering and access guarantees.

options.text: For each row, perform an iterative binary search for x; stop on a match, otherwise return false after the last row.
options.feedback: A binary search needs its own ordered range; independently sorted rows do not imply global row-major order.

options.text: Copy each row into a temporary buffer before running its binary search, discarding the buffer before the next row.
options.feedback: Copying preserves correctness but adds avoidable work and storage for each row.

options.text: Treat row-major indices as one sorted array and binary-search across all cells.
options.feedback: For [[1,8],[2,4]], x=8, a virtual search can inspect 2 then 4 and report absent because the combined order is not sorted.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For target-method, choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Analyze sequential iterative search of every row, worst case with no match. Random cell access and integer operations are constant time; do not copy rows or use recursion. Input storage and returned result storage are excluded; all temporary buffers and call stacks are included.
constraints: Use worst-case bounds. Count all working memory including any stack; exclude supplied inputs and the scalar result.

options.text: O(r log(c + 1)) time, O(1) auxiliary space
O(r log(c + 1)) time, O(r*c + 1) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Perform a logarithmic indexed search independently in each row.
details: An absent query can force r searches, each over c ordered entries. Their sum is O(r log(c+1)). Search one row at a time with the same scalar bounds, so peak auxiliary storage remains O(1).
“O(r log(c + 1)) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: A binary search needs its own ordered range; independently sorted rows do not imply global row-major order.
“O(r log(c + 1)) time, O(r*c + 1) auxiliary space”: Rows are reused directly and searched sequentially, so no r*c auxiliary matrix is copied.
“O(1) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: An absent value can require all r independent row searches, each with logarithmic c-dependent probes.
